issues.legal_issue: A widow’s possession of her deceased husband’s estate in lieu of dower does not give her dower claim priority over his other unsecured creditors.
material_facts: The widow possessed a house belonging to her deceased husband in lieu of her outstanding dower claim.
The deceased left other debts, including a debt owed to the decree-holder.
The house had not been charged or mortgaged in favour of the widow or any creditor.
The executing court had ordered the house sold subject to the widow’s claim, treating her as having priority over unsecured creditors.
issues.conclusion: The widow’s objection to the execution had no substance. The property was to be sold and the proceeds distributed rateably among the decree-holders and the widow.
issues.legal_principle: Dower is a debt arising from the marriage contract. It ranks ahead of bequests and inheritance, but it has no inherent priority over other contractual debts or unsecured creditors. The Quranic text in Surai-Nissa, Ruku 4, requires payment of dower in preference to bequests and inheritance but does not establish priority over other creditors; the Mubsoot Sarkhasi and Fatwa-e-Alamgiri support payment of debts before distribution to legatees and heirs. The Court adopted the principles stated in Tyabji’s Muhammadan Law and approved Ameer Ammal v. Sankaranarayanan Chetty (I.L.R. 25 Mad. 658), Meer Meher Ally v. Mst. Amanee (11 W.R. 212), Maina Bibi v. Wasi Ahmad (I.L.R. 41 All. 538), Hamira Bibi v. Zubaida Bibi (A.I.R. 1916 P.C. 46), and Imtiaz Begum v. Abdul Karim Khan (A.I.R. 1930 All. 881). It explained Maina Bibi v. Chaudhri Vakil Ahmad (52 I.A. 145) as not placing the widow above other creditors, and disapproved Kulsum Bibi v. Shiam Sunder Lal (A.I.R. 1936 All. 600), Mst. Ghafooran v. Ram Chandra Das (A.I.R. 1934 All. 168), and Mohamed Turabuddin v. Yasin Begum (17 D.L.R. 224) insofar as they supported priority.

rule.if: estate_creditor_priority_proceeding and widow_holds_property_for_dower and husband_left_unsecured_debts and no_security_created_for_widow

predicates.estate_creditor_priority_proceeding: A creditor pursued execution against property left by a deceased debtor, raising the priority of claims against the estate.
predicates.widow_holds_property_for_dower: A widow possessed property of her deceased husband in lieu of an outstanding dower claim.
predicates.husband_left_unsecured_debts: The deceased husband left debts owed to creditors who held no security over the property.
predicates.no_security_created_for_widow: The husband had not charged or mortgaged the property in favour of the widow.

issues.definition: When a widow holds her deceased husband’s property for dower in an estate-creditor priority proceeding, the estate has unsecured debts, and the husband created no security for her, her dower debt ranks equally with the other unsecured debts.
